speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I know the situation in Myanmar is evolving and there may be other Members of Parliament who are following this closely, so, I will give somewhat of a more comprehensive answer.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The detentions occurred in the country’s capital just before the new Union Parliament was scheduled to convene.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The military has imposed a one-year State of Emergency, formed a State Administration Council and apparently appointed new Cabinet members.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There have been large scale protests against the military and these protests have taken place across Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There are media reports that some protestors have been injured and, sadly, one succumbed to her injuries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There were also reports of armed vehicle movements and the deployment of troops in several cities, including clashes between security forces and demonstrators as well as the arrests of civil servants and students.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Internet services have been cut several times, making access to information difficult.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, I think, right now, Internet access is disrupted.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We urge the authorities to exercise utmost restraint to avoid further injuries and loss of lives and we hope they will take urgent steps to de-escalate the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There should be no violence against unarmed civilians and we hope that there will be peaceful resolution and national reconciliation in Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In this respect, I also hope that President Win Myint, State Counsellor Daw Aung San Suu Kyi and the other detainees will be released so that they can engage in discussions and negotiations in good faith.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The stakeholders in Myanmar must find a long-term peaceful political solution, including a return to its path of democratic transition.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: If the situation continues to escalate, there will be serious consequences for Myanmar and, indeed, for our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Amidst these escalating tensions, our Embassy in Yangon has maintained regular contact with Singaporeans in Myanmar, particularly those who are e-registered with our Embassy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have advised Singaporeans in Myanmar to avoid public gatherings and demonstrations, to abide by all local laws and regulations and to monitor the news closely.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There are currently about 500 Singaporeans who have registered with MFA and we urge other Singaporeans who may not yet have registered with us to do so quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Given the initial news of airport closures, suspension of flights and the disruption of mobile and Internet services, several Singaporeans have been in contact with our Embassy, including some who were considering returning to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Yangon International Airport reopened on 4 February and the regular weekly relief flights between Yangon and Singapore have been able to operate as scheduled.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So far, only 17 Singaporeans have chosen to return home on the flights on 5 and 12 February.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The suspension of telecommunications connectivity at this time is deeply concerning, especially when access to information is critical.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans in Myanmar who require consular assistance may have some difficulty reaching us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We thus hope that there would be no further disruptions to mobile and Internet connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MFA will continue to maintain close contact with the Singaporean community in Myanmar and we stand ready to render appropriate consular assistance to any Singaporeans in distress.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore has always upheld the principle that the future of Myanmar has to be determined by her own people.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have supported Myanmar’s difficult democratic transition thus far.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are gravely concerned about the latest developments in Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Myanmar was already facing serious socio-economic challenges, made worse by the onset of COVID-19 last year and the continued armed ethnic insurgencies and, of course, Members are familiar with the situation of the refugees from Rakhine state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: All these uncertainties, including from the latest developments, not only damage the prospects for Myanmar but also damage the broader stability of our region.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN has a longstanding policy of non-interference in the internal affairs of our member states.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Nevertheless, a Statement was issued quickly by the ASEAN Chair to reflect the seriousness with which ASEAN views the developments in Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Statement emphasised and reaffirmed the importance of the principles enshrined in the ASEAN Charter, including adherence to the principles of democracy, the rule of law and good governance, respect for and protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It also called for dialogue, reconciliation and the return to normalcy in accordance with the will of the people of Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: All ASEAN member states are expected to uphold the principles enshrined in the ASEAN Charter and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But ASEAN also operates by the principles of consensus and non-interference in the internal affairs of ASEAN member states.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Nevertheless, I believe ASEAN can play a discreet constructive role in facilitating a return to normalcy and stability in Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: ASEAN’s external partners, particularly the major powers, have an important role to play as well.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Their perspectives are clear – you would have read the various statements that have been issued in the last two weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Engagement, rather than isolation, will go further in ameliorating this crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Unfortunately, the recent political developments in Myanmar will inevitably further complicate the situation in Rakhine State and of the refugees from that state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Therefore, it will also inevitably delay the efforts to commence the repatriation of displaced persons, considering that we are also dealing with the COVID-19 pandemic which is affecting Myanmar.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, it will take time to reach a long-term political solution in Myanmar as well as in Rakhine State, in particular.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we do hope that all parties would give due consideration to the urgent humanitarian needs of the displaced persons, both in terms of immediate assistance and the need to improve ground conditions in the refugee camps.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I appreciate there are many moving parts, but what are the strategic aspects and the Minister's predictions, if one can call it that, in light of the military coup ensuing in Myanmar presently?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But the Member has raised several fundamental strategic questions and, with your permission, Mr Speaker, let me take a step back and go back to first principles.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our starting point has to be that every country's politics and destiny should be determined by its own people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Just as in Singapore, we will not tolerate foreign interference in our politics.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Similarly, we do not seek to interfere in others' domestic affairs.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is a principle we hold fast to and, in fact, this is a foundational principle of ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The next point I want to make is because many people do not appreciate the many moving parts that the Member has just described.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Myanmar is the 40th largest country in the world by size, twice the land area of Vietnam.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It has a mostly young, intelligent, hard-working, disciplined population of 55 million.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Many of us here have colleagues or friends from Myanmar and you will know that these descriptions I have used are accurate.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Fifty-five percent of their people are below the age of 30.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you look at the map, you will also realise that Myanmar occupies a very unique and critical geo-strategic position at the crossroads of India, China, Indochina and, in fact, has also a portal into Southeast Asia as a whole.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Both India and China have had a long history of engagement with Myanmar, over millennia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And 200 years ago, the British Raj battled with the last Burmese dynasty for control of the region around the Bay of Bengal.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, the Rakhine state was one of the first areas to fall to the British and the Burmese were forced to cede that area to the British Raj.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: During World War II, Myanmar was a major theatre of operations because of its strategic location.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: China today shares a border with Myanmar that is more than 2,000 kilometres in length.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Its trade with Myanmar last year was US$10.2 billion, making China, Myanmar's largest trading partner – larger, in fact, than even its trade with the rest of ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In short, due to its geography, Myanmar is no stranger to strategic rivalries, nor is it unfamiliar with the contest for influence from its larger neighbours.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And it has long sought to pursue a realist paradigm and an independent foreign policy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And for that reason, I believe, Myanmar chose to become part of ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is also worth reminding everyone here that Myanmar is a union, one that, since independence – and mind you, at independence, they were far ahead of Singapore – since their independence, they have struggled to forge a national identity that reflects its ethnic diversity.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Racial and religious divisions run deep in the country with eight major national ethnic races and 135 ethnic groups.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It has manifested in multiple long-running armed ethnic conflicts.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And the refugee situation in Rakhine State – which remains unresolved to this day – is in fact a complex inter-communal issue with deep historical roots, going back in time.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Given the risk of balkanisation, given that milieu, you would understand why Myanmar's national reconciliation and peace process is so essential and yet so fragile; and any prolonged instability in Myanmar will also affect Southeast Asia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Actually, Myanmar has come a long way in the last decade.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And you may be aware that Singaporean companies have looked towards Myanmar for economic opportunities, new market access and to diversify our growth.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I think what is interesting is that, of that figure I have cited, the major proportion of our investments in Myanmar, have in fact occurred in the last five years under the NLD government.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I want to stress that companies made these investment decisions on commercial grounds.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: They did not do so because of political influence or political suggestion on our part.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I believe that the commercial companies saw promising opportunities in a Myanmar that was undergoing democratic transition.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I say all these, in order to head off suggestions that we should now interfere on political grounds with commercial decisions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But in the same way, I am sure companies making commercial decisions and investment decisions will also pay attention to the political context of the venue in which they are seeking to invest in.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And therefore, what has just happened is a major setback for its economy and for its ability to attract foreign investments.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The current volatile operating environment, including a report that a foreign national had been arrested, will certainly affect the investment outlook and undermine business confidence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Our own businessmen are aware of these downside risks, and I have no doubt that Singaporean businesses are also re-evaluating their risk profile and their exposure to this market.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have had conversations with several counterparts – the US, Germany and others.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The World Bank estimates that around a quarter of the population in Myanmar lives below the poverty line.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And in fact, this has been worsened by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And so, in all my discussions and phone calls, I have said that we should not embark on widespread, generalised and indiscriminate sanctions because the people who will suffer most will be the ordinary people in Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In some, it is in recognition of this complex collage – historical, geo-strategic, economic, demographic factors – that we hope fervently for national reconciliation in Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This is inimical to our own national interests, and of course, we will deal with this firmly in accordance to the law.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Regional instability precipitated by events, like in Myanmar, can impinge on Singapore's interests.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I understand that there is a special meeting of Foreign Ministers of Southeast Asian nations being called to discuss the situation in Myanmar.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Will Singapore be represented at this meeting and what are the key objectives that Singapore would like to see achieved at this meeting?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: If so, given the high possibility that the US and other western nations may slap further sanctions on the Myanmar military and its companies, is the Government providing the necessary advice and assistance to companies, which may get caught up in this, so that they can reduce their exposure?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You would realise that the difficulty there is we need consensus before the meeting can even take place.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Having said that, however, I can assure you that there has been an intense flurry of communications, bilateral and group, amongst the Foreign Ministers in ASEAN.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The main thing is not to make things worse, and not to be inflammatory.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I have also answered earlier on our advice to businesses that you have to take into account political risk, and social and political dynamics before making investment decisions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am sure all our companies are currently re-evaluating their position.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But again, I want to emphasise that it is crucial for us in both good times and bad times to maintain this separation between politics and business, and let businesses make commercial decisions and investment decisions on their own merits.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And I think this is a good time for us to maintain that discipline.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, no, I will not give specific advice to companies, but I will make, to the maximum extent possible, all information available in this House and beyond, so that people can make their own commercial and investment decisions.
